figures.finding: The age of majority is twenty-one full Gregorian years; from then a person is fully competent to perform legal transactions unless guardianship or trusteeship over his property was continued before it.
figures.applies: Guardianship of Property Law, Legislative Decree No. 7 of 1986, art. 13 (the "legal age" the Civil Code, Decree No. 19 of 2001, art. 73-75, defers to).

sources.said: Article -13- The age of majority is twenty-one full Gregorian years. Anyone who reaches the age of majority shall be considered fully competent to perform legal transactions unless guardianship or trusteeship over their property has been continuously established before that,

figures.finding: A minor's property is under a guardian's or trustee's management, overseen by the Council of Guardianship over the Funds of Minors; the Council may authorise a minor of sixteen to enter an employment contract under the Labour Law, may have it ended in his interest, and the authorised minor manages his own wages and other earnings from that work, within the obligations it creates; from eighteen the Council may let him manage some or all of his funds. No share of earnings is fixed to be set aside. The rule is for any employment contract, so it reaches writing or directing for an employer as well as acting (reading).

value.binding: the Council of Guardianship over the Funds of Minors authorises a minor of 16+ to contract for employment (art. 44)

figures.applies: Guardianship of Property Law (Decree No. 7 of 1986), arts. 39, 44.

sources.said: Article -44- The Council may grant authorization to a minor who has reached the age of sixteen to enter into an employment contract in accordance with the provisions of the Labour Law. Upon the request of the Directorate or one of the concerned parties, the contract may be terminated in consideration of the minor's best interests, their future, or any apparent interests. In this case, the minor shall be entitled to manage the earnings from their work, whether wages or otherwise, ... Article -39- The Council may, after hearing the statements of the legal guardians or trustees, grant unrestricted or conditional permission to a minor who has reached the age of eighteen to take control of some or all of their funds for management,

figures.finding: There is no rule or permit for a child performer: the private-sector Labour Law forbids employing anyone under fifteen, with no exception for artistic work, so a film or stage role for a child under fifteen as employment is barred (reading); a juvenile (fifteen to eighteen) works at most six hours a day, never more than four in a row, with at least an hour's break, stays no more than seven hours on site, never at night, on weekly rest days or public holidays, and only with his parents' or guardian's approval and a medical check. The same reaches a young writer or director employed on a production.
figures.applies: Labour Law for the Private Sector, Law No. 36 of 2012, arts. 23-27.

sources.said: a juvenile means every person of fifteen years of age but not exceeding eighteen years of age. Article (24):It is prohibited to employ anyone who is less than fifteen years of age. Article (25):Juveniles shall not be employed to actively work for a period exceeding six hours a day. They shall not be permitted to remain in the place of employment for more than seven consecutive hours. The hours of work shall be interrupted by one or more intervals for rest and having a meal, the total of which shall not be less than one hour. Such interval or intervals shall be so arranged that juveniles shall not work for more than four consecutive hours.Article (26):Juveniles shall not be employed during the night nor shall they be employed during the weekly days of rest or public holidays. Article (27):Before employing a juvenile, an employer shall comply with the following: He shall ascertain the parents' or guardians' approval of the juvenile’s employment. A medical check of the juvenile shall be conducted to confirm his medical fitness for work.

figures.finding: A Bahraini of eighteen with no legal restriction may carry on commercial business; a minor under guardianship or trusteeship may not engage in business until eighteen and the Council's permission, and where a minor owns funds in a business the court decides whether he stays in it.

value.minorBusiness: from 18 with the Council of Guardianship's permission while still a minor (under 21)
value.minorHoldings: court may liquidate or continue (Law of Commerce art. 11)

figures.applies: Law of Commerce (Decree No. 7 of 1987, as amended), arts. 10-11; Guardianship of Property Law art. 39. The Commercial Companies Law (Decree No. 21 of 2001) on directors was not read.

sources.said: Article 10Every Bahraini who is 18 years of age with no legal restrictions imposed against him personally or against the type of commercial business he is undertaking, shall have the capacity to undertake commercial business. Article 111) If a minor or an incompetent person owns funds in a commercial business, the Court may order the liquidation of his share and withdrawal of his funds from such business

The minor, whether subject to guardianship or trusteeship, is not allowed to engage in business activities until they reach the age of eighteen and receive permission from the Council, either unrestricted or conditional.

figures.finding: Tamkeen's film and television support (up to 50%, milestone based) goes only to Bahrain-based enterprises with an active commercial registration owning the project's IP, so the applicant is a company and the person behind it needs the capacity to trade (eighteen, see companies); it names no age of its own.

value.applicant: Bahrain-based enterprise with an active CR/license

sources.said: Eligibility • Bahrain-based enterprises with an active CR/ ... • Has complete IP ownership of the project
